answer: Identity verification binds agent to 64 GB physical DRAM. Verifier issues seed; worker runs sequential 64-byte cache-line traversals over pseudo-random RAM offsets across memory bridge. Zenith latency limits prevent storage swapping. Agent applies cryptographic seal to final hash chain, returning proof within 40 milliseconds. Verifier validates seal; timeout or bit mismatch drops agent and slashes deposit. Single machine cannot harbor ghost identities because bus saturation blocks time-multiplexing; running 1000 sybils demands 64 TB dedicated RAM costing $95,000.
